grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a home staple, and the all-butter shortcrust pastry and crème fraîche are on the allowed list.

supermarket.reason: Turnips, leeks, ready-rolled pastry, crème fraîche and Cheddar are everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: A tart tin, frying pan, bowl and whisk are ordinary kit, and lining a tin with ready-rolled pastry suits a confident beginner.

works.reason: Softening the turnips with the leeks first, using a three-egg custard for a 23cm tin and baking on a preheated tray at 200°C gives a set, well-seasoned quiche for four.

honest_times.reason: Peeling and dicing 400g of turnip, slicing the leeks, lining the tin and sweating the veg fits about 25 minutes, and the 35 to 40 minute bake plus resting matches the 50 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, nothing unlisted is used, and the names match their ids.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm turnip and leek quiche suits early February, and the turnips make up the bulk of the filling.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with sensible cues such as 'a slight wobble in the middle'.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling lunch of eggs, cheese and plenty of vegetables in pastry that a family would happily eat again.
